text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Goran Persson on Monday talked rates up and housing institutions took quick advantage of the move to raise their interest rates. Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said he was concerned about the increase in debt yields across Europe.

- A 36-year-old man in Kristianstad was arrested on Monday and charged with two murders. He has said that he is possibly involved in more than just the two incidents that date back to 1985. He is accused of murdered a 27-year-old woman and a 35-year-old woman, both from Kristianstad.
- Only eight of 76 European Union motions proposed for the ruling Social Democrats congress in September were positive towards Swedish membership of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).

- Media group Kinnevik posted a sharply lower profit in 1996 of 159 million crowns after financial items against a profit of one billion crowns a year earlier. This was despite a one-off gain of 600 million crowns from the sale of telecommunications company Netcom.

- A tax proposal presented on Monday suggested lower taxes on car repairs, restaurants and other services to give lower prices that would support the services sector and provide up to 40,000 new jobs. On the other hand it suggested raising taxes on tobacco to collect a further 1.7 billion crowns.

- The Nordic finance and banking scene is continuing to change with provincial Swedish bank Ostgota Enskilda Bank being taken over by Denmark's Den Danske Bank at a price of 50.50 crowns a share. Den Danske Bank's managing director Peter Straarup said a good bank was always expensive.

- Finance and real estate company Lundbergforetagen has accepted a 2.2 billion crown cash bid from Den Danske Bank for its 77 percent stake of provincial Swedish bank Ostgota Enskilda Bank OGB.ST. Ostgota Enskilda is based in Linkoping, 200 kms south of Stockholm, employs 550 people and has 29 branches. Den Danske Bank will pay 50.50 crowns for each share.

- The Lundberg group will use the 2.2 billion crowns from selling its Ostgota Enskilda stake to make new investments in Sweden. President and main owner Fredrik Lundberg said his philosophy was to work in a longterm context and the group will probably become involved in a number of companies. Lundberg also has a slice of forestry group MoDo and 15 percent of construction group NCC.

- A government-sponsored review of the tax system in the service inudstry proposes changes which could mean 40,000 new jobs and a 10 percent reduction of prices in restaurants, barber shops, taxis and car repairs. These changes, which would reduce state revenues by 3.6 billion crowns, would be financed partly by increasing the tax on tobacco products and reducing the basic tax deduction for individuals.
